But because the seat of the thoughts is in the breast, in the rational, which is the priestly vesture of the breast, the clean thoughts of the elect are expressed. The onyx stones therefore and the gems adorn the ephod and the rational when the acts and thoughts of the holy Fathers are distinguished also by miracles. Or in the onyx stones, which are said to be of the colour of blood, the merits of martyrdom added to good works are signified.
04_interl3991: not in part: if we desire the fellowship of the angels, we ought to imitate their life on earth, as far as our hurtful bodies do not hold us back.
04_interl3992: of the heavenly fatherland, to the likeness of which the Church is commanded to be built
04_marg1458: AND THEY SHALL MAKE ME etc. BEDE. The Lord showed Moses the tabernacle on the mountain, and the vessels consecrated for its service, because to him who abode with him so long he openly showed with how great humility, piety and purity the angelic powers rejoice to obey. These are the perfect tabernacle of him who has always dwelt in them. Whose likeness of life also, and common conversation before God, is promised to us in the resurrection: whoever of us now strive to imitate their life, namely by praising and loving God and neighbour, and calling even enemies to God; to whom it is said: But you, brethren, are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit. The tabernacle therefore shown to Moses on the mountain is the heavenly fatherland, which then consisted of the angels alone, but after the ascension received a glorious multitude of holy souls.
04_marg1459: BEDE. We ought to imitate the angels by loving God and neighbour. They too come to the help of the wretched, if not of angels, who are all blessed, at least of men. They are humble, they are meek, peaceable, they obey the divine precepts. Imitate these as far as you can, that you may build in yourself a sanctuary for the Lord according to the pattern which was shown on the mountain, that God may both dwell in you now, and after this life bring you into that tabernacle which you imitate.
04_marg1460: OF ALL THE VESSELS etc. BEDE. The vessels of the tabernacle are the several persons of the angels, of whom Jerusalem, the mother of us all, consists in true peace and unity.
04_interl3994: the body of Christ, which was corrupted by no contagion of sin, whose length was the endurance of the passion
04_interl3995: with most pure members, though "in the likeness of sinful flesh"
04_marg1461: AND THUS YOU SHALL MAKE etc. BEDE. An ark is commanded to be made, in which the incarnation of Christ is figured, in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. It is framed of setim wood, which is light and incorruptible and differs little in quality from the white thorn, because the body of Christ consists of members clean from all vice. This wood is like thorns, because he came not in sinful flesh, but "in the likeness of sinful flesh".
04_interl3997: the teaching and the working of Christ, of which one was not without the other
04_interl3998: We do not have the full cubit, because we cannot imitate his works to the full.
04_interl3999: because he bore long-sufferingly the slowness of the disciples
04_marg1462: BEDE. It is asked of what size is this cubit which Moses set in the tabernacle, Noe in the ark. According to Josephus: it is not to be thought that a Jew endowed with talent, most learned in the divine and secular Scriptures, could have been ignorant of this. He says therefore: The ark was made of a length of five palms, a breadth of three. Whence it is plain that he designates that cubit which two palms make.
04_interl4000: the breadth of charity, which is one but divided into two commandments
04_interl4001: of the charity by which he took care to unite his own
04_interl4002: because in this life we are not able either to love God perfectly or to comprehend how much he loves us
04_marg1463: BEDE. The breadth of one cubit is for the dispensation of the Lord's charity, by which he took care to unite the elect in God. Whence: That they may be one in us. And a little after: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them. It has also a half, because in this life we are not able either to love God perfectly or to comprehend the love which God has toward us, because we love in part, as we know in part. The ark therefore has one cubit and a half, because the Lord loves us with a single goodness, to be joined to himself and the Father, and embraces with equally kind goodness the capacity of our love such as it can be in this life, until we enter into his vision, where we may love him with all our heart.
04_interl4003: For the single hope by which we await the coming of the glory of the future resurrection; or because he admonishes us to rejoice amid adversities for the sake of the rewards to come.
04_marg1464: Mystically. The length of the ark suggests the long-suffering of Christ, and the patience with which he conversed among men. The breadth, the breadth of the charity with which he came to us and dwelt with us. The height, the hope of the sublimity to come, by which he foresaw that after his passion he was to be glorified, or would glorify. Whence the length of two cubits, namely for the teaching and the works by which he shone in the world. Whence: "Which Jesus began to do and to teach." And elsewhere: "How came this man by this wisdom and miracles?" But that the ark had a half in its length can signify the slowness of human frailty, which could not worthily grasp the sublime words or works of Christ. Whence: "These things his disciples did not know at the first" etc., namely his deeds. And elsewhere: "This word was hid from them" etc. The ark therefore had two cubits of length, because he appeared in the flesh renowned in word and deed. But the half cubit, because he bore long-sufferingly the slowness of the disciples.
04_marg1465: THE HEIGHT, A CUBIT etc. BEDE. The ark has a cubit in height, because Christ knew most fully, while he was in corruptible flesh, how great a glory was to be either for himself or for his members. It has also a half, because he willingly took into himself the devotion of our flesh; because we love the fatherland to come with devout intention, but do not yet perfectly grasp what its happiness is, and this little we have only from him.
04_interl4004: because his humanity was full of power within, and without showed forth the works of the Holy Ghost
04_interl4005: because he waited for the time when he would overcome, for us, the death he had taken up together with the author of death, and ascend to the Father as victor, crowned with glory and honour
04_interl4006: the four books of the Gospels, which are compared to rings, because the eternal Wisdom of God which they preach, which man received, neither begins nor ends
04_interl4008: because the sacraments of the incarnation are spread through all the regions of the world, and the Gospel is preached
04_interl4009: because two evangelists cleaved to him while he preached in the flesh, two others cleaved to Christ after the resurrection and ascension
04_interl4010: John and Matthew, who cleaved to Christ as he preached
04_interl4012: namely Mark and Luke, who, believing afterward, were made disciples of the apostles
04_interl4014: the doctors, who carry God about by preaching
04_interl4015: because they ought to be pure and strong
04_interl4019: because it is needful that those who preach heavenly things to others never hold back the mind from the memory of sacred Scripture, or the hands from the observance of the commandments
04_interl4020: that they may never cease from reading
04_marg1466: AND FOUR RINGS etc. GREGORY. The ark is the Church. The four golden rings at the four corners are the four books of the Gospel, by which it is preached through the four parts of the world; the bars of setim wood, which are put into the rings for carrying, are the strong and persevering doctors, who, ever cleaving to the sacred books, proclaim the unity of the Church. To carry the ark with the bars is for good doctors, by preaching, to bring the Church to the rude minds of unbelievers. These are commanded to be overlaid with gold, that when they preach to others they may shine with the brightness of knowledge. These shall always be in the rings, nor ever be drawn out, that those who keep watch in the office of preaching may never withdraw from the study of reading. For the bars are commanded always to be in the rings of the ark for this, that when the ark is to be carried no delay may arise over putting in the bars; because when something spiritual is asked of the pastor, it is shameful if he seeks to learn then, when he ought to untie the question; but let the bars cleave to the rings, that the doctors, ever meditating the words of the Lord, may lift the ark of the Testament without delay, and teach whatever is needful. Whence Peter: Being ready always to satisfy every one that asketh a reason of that hope and faith which is in us.
04_marg1467: TWO RINGS etc. BEDE. Because in the figure of the four living creatures, two, which are signified by the man and the calf, signified the passion and death; two, which by the lion and the eagle, the victory, namely by which he destroyed death. For as man, God appeared made mortal through the incarnation. As calf, he was offered for us on the altar of the cross. Again, he was made lion by overcoming death, eagle by ascending. There are therefore two rings on one side and two on the other, because two evangelists suggest the taking up of human frailty in the Lord; and two the victory by which he triumphed over the frailty taken up and over death. For as it were the left side had two rings, when two evangelists figured the incarnation and passion of Christ; the right side also two, when two others expressed the resurrection and ascension, which pertain to the glory of the life to come.
04_interl4021: because we ought to speak and believe of the incarnation only those things which the Lord himself deigns to reveal to us through the authors of sacred Scripture
04_marg1468: THE TESTIMONY WHICH etc. BEDE. Of which the Apostle says: "And after the second veil, the tabernacle, which is called the holy of holies: having a golden censer, and the ark of the testament covered about on every part with gold, in which was a golden pot that had manna, and the rod of Aaron, that had blossomed, and the tables of the testament." The golden pot therefore in the ark having manna is the holy soul in Christ, having in itself all the fullness of the godhead. The rod of Aaron, which had blossomed after being cut, is the unconquered power of the priesthood, of which it is said: "The sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness"; which, cut down for a time by death, flowered again living on the morning of the resurrection, and was made known as to remain for ever inviolable and unfading: for Christ rising from the dead dieth now no more. The tables of the testament in the ark designate all the knowledge in Christ of the Father's secrets, and the power of judgments. For in them was inscribed both the faith of the godhead, which created and rules the world; and the commandments by which God must be served; and the discretion of judgment, by which he would condemn those who hate him and reward those who love him. This then is the testimony which God gave Moses to be put in the ark, when he signified to us that we must confess in Christ the truth of flesh and soul and Word; and showed that flesh itself glorified after the passion and resurrection, and exalted to the eternal dignity of king and pontiff; and taught that he alone is privy to the Father's secrets, as being of the same majesty with the Father, the judge of all ages.
04_interl4022: the propitiatory is Christ, of whom the Apostle: Whom he hath proposed to be a propitiation, through faith in his blood.
04_interl4023: "Mercy exalteth itself above judgment"; whence: "The Lord is sweet to all, and his tender mercies are over" etc.
04_interl4024: namely a plate sufficient to cover the ark
04_interl4025: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO A PROPITIATORY. BEDE. The propitiatory was a golden plate of the same measure as the ark; so called because there God, appearing to Moses and speaking with him, was propitiated toward the people; and it signifies mercy. Whence it was well upon the ark, because his tender mercies are over all his works.
04_interl4026: the two testaments, of which one proclaims the incarnation to come, the other the incarnation accomplished
04_marg1469: TWO CHERUBIMS ALSO etc. For the fellowship of angelic peace, which cannot be had among fewer than two. And Cherubim signifies the angelic host. But the angels contemplate Christ in the highest concord and quiet. Whence, their faces turned toward each other, they look upon the propitiatory, because they understand that they have that beatitude by the grace of God.
04_interl4028: as it were looking upon the propitiatory they overshadow it, because they ascribe their happiness to the grace of God, from whom they have received that they can will nothing evil
04_interl4029: because they offer to the service of the Creator all the power of their nature, by which they deserve to dwell on high and to pass through the place of that fatherland with light and joyful journey
04_marg1470: The two cherubim, which are called fullness of knowledge, are the two Testaments, of which one stands at one end of the propitiatory, the other at the other: because what the Old began to promise by prophesying of the incarnation of Christ, the New relates as perfectly fulfilled. They are made of the purest gold, because both Testaments are written with pure and simple truth. They spread their wings and cover the oracles, because we, who are the oracle of God, are protected from impending faults by the instruction of sacred Scripture; and while we look on it carefully, we are veiled by its wings from the error of ignorance. They look at each other, their faces turned toward the propitiatory, because the Testaments disagree in nothing, and they behold each other, because what one promises the other shows forth. And they see the propitiatory, that is, the mediator of God and men, set between them. For they would turn their faces away from each other if the one promised what the other denied.
04_marg1471: In the singular number it is called cherub, but in the plural 'cherubim'. But the Greek custom put cherubin of the neuter gender, the letter 'm' being changed into 'n'. But Jerome put it also in the masculine gender: duos Cherubim aureos etc., not duo Cherubim aurea. And it is interpreted multitude of knowledge, or understanding of knowledge: which rightly befits the angels, who, strangers to every impulse of impure thought, cleave to the vision of the Creator. Moses is commanded to make wings in the figure of the Cherubim, which the licence of painters also imitates, that the angels may be signified to have their seat on high, and to run whithersoever with light flight. Which is also promised us without doubt after the resurrection, when we are clothed with a spiritual body. The two Cherubim look at each other, because the two Testaments disagree in nothing in their witness to the truth which they preach. They turn their faces toward the propitiatory, because they greatly commend the mercy of God, which is the only hope of the world. And therefore they are on both sides of the oracle, because they fill the times before the incarnation and those after it with the preaching of spiritual knowledge. To these also the name of multiplied knowledge is fitting, because Scripture is full of spiritual knowledge, which, from the time it began to be made, is increased and multiplied. Whence: Many shall pass over, and knowledge shall be manifold. For Moses had a fuller knowledge than the patriarchs. Whence: I that appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and my name Adonai I did not show them; understand: as to thee. David also says: "I have understood more than all my teachers." And elsewhere: "The uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me." The Lord also declares that the apostles know greater things than the prophets, saying: Many prophets and just men have desired to see the things that you see etc. And to them he promises a greater knowledge after the ascension: "I have yet many things to say to you" etc. In the future also he promises that he will reveal himself more, saying: "And I will manifest myself to him." Rightly therefore Cherubim is called multiplied knowledge, because in each Testament, more and more as time goes on, the knowledge of the truth becomes known to the faithful. Rightly the Cherubim are said to overshadow the propitiatory, because the Testaments, as knowledge grows and is multiplied, preach the propitiation of the Saviour; and with thankful voices, as with wings spread for flying, they never cease to honour it. For because the words of those who speak together, as it were flying through the air, come from the mouth of the speakers to the heart of the hearers, they are well designated by wings spread and fitted for flying.
04_interl4033: to which they attribute all their happiness
04_interl4036: because through the grace of propitiation he appears to men after the error of transgression and teaches the way
04_interl4037: namely in an angelic vision, not in his own substance
04_interl4039: the Church, to which God testifies his will
04_marg1472: THENCE WILL I GIVE ORDERS AND WILL SPEAK etc. BEDE. Over the propitiatory, because it was done through the grace of God's propitiation that he deigned to appear to men after transgression, and to show the way of truth after error. And he speaks from the midst of the Cherubim, because he appeared and spoke to Moses through an angelic vision, and not in his own substance. Whence: The law was set because of transgressions, being ordained by angels etc. Again he speaks from the midst of the Cherubim, because he instructs with harmonious voice through the words of each Testament; or because through the Son, who appeared in the flesh in the midst of the two Testaments, he showed the Father's will. Whence Habacuc says: In the midst of two living creatures thou shalt be made known.
04_marg1473: In the ark the Church also can be figured, which is built of incorruptible wood, that is, holy souls; and, spread through the four parts of the world in the faith of the Gospel, awaits from God the crown of life, having in itself the tables of the Testament in the continual meditation of the Law of God, and the golden pot with the manna in the faith of the Lord's incarnation, and the rod of Aaron which blossomed in sharing the Lord's kingdom and priesthood. Whence: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood." It has the propitiatory above, that it may know it has received all good things from divine grace. And the Cherubim of glory on the propitiatory, namely the angelic guards, by which it is helped, God being propitious. Or the Testaments, by which it is instructed how it should live, and should seek from God the help of living. And the Cherubim are above the propitiatory in the way that the city, that is, the Church, is said to be set upon the mountain, that is, Christ: not higher than he, but because it advances, sustained by his guard. The ark has the Cherubim above the propitiatory, because the angelic mysteries or the divine words help the Church the more truly, the more they stand firm on the foundation of the highest truth.
04_interl4040: Scripture, which receives no corruption of falsehood
04_interl4041: with the strong words and deeds of the fathers
04_interl4042: the purity and innocence which Scripture teaches must be had
04_interl4045: because charity is one and simple
04_interl4046: namely in hope of the future reward
04_marg1474: THOU SHALT MAKE A TABLE ALSO etc. BEDE. The table of setim wood is Scripture, compacted of the strong words and deeds of the Fathers, which, while it shows the eternal joys and how one comes to them, supplies the food of life. It has length when it suggests perseverance in the religion begun; breadth, when the breadth of charity; height, when the hope of the resurrection. The length is of two cubits, because the active conversation consists chiefly in two virtues, namely purity and innocence. Whence: "Religion clean and undefiled before God and the Father, is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their tribulation" etc. For in saying "to visit the fatherless and widows" etc., he shows all that we owe mercifully to neighbours in need. But in adding "and to keep one's self unspotted from this world", he expresses all the things by which one ought to live chastely. Whence: Let your loins be girt, and lamps burning in your hands etc. But what follows: And you yourselves like to men who wait for their lord etc., signifies the height of the table, that is, the hope of the future reward. That the table has one cubit in breadth shows the unity of charity which the whole Old and New Testament preaches. For one and simple is the charity by which we are commanded to love God, and neighbour, and enemies, although by right distinction God in the first place, enemies in the last; for the difference of their merits an unequal measure of love is to be spent on neighbours. For Jacob loved all his sons, but Joseph, for the merit of his innocence, above the rest. Whence: "The king brought me into the cellar of wine", and "he set in order charity in me".
04_marg1475: IN HEIGHT A CUBIT etc. BEDE. That the height has a cubit and a half: the cubit, as in the breadth, signifies the unity of heavenly hope, by which we await God from heaven to reward us. For though, for the diversity of merits, there are many mansions in the Father's house, yet one is the kingdom of heaven in which all the elect are received. But the half is the beginning of contemplation, which some of the saints deserved to enjoy even while set in the flesh, to whom it was given not only to hope for heavenly things but even, by seeing, partly to foretaste them; in whom the table of the tabernacle, that is, the divine Scripture, by which the Church is ever refreshed, adds a half in height over the cubit of common hope, because it foreshows the joys shown to them before they are rendered; because what is done hastily and in passing is figured by a half, not by a full cubit.
04_interl4049: because Scripture shines with the sense of heavenly wisdom, and they who composed it were renowned in life and speech
04_interl4050: because the teaching of the word is given us through the clean mouths of preachers
04_interl4051: because they reprove all hurtful and idle things
04_interl4052: because the tongue of the preachers promises the hearers themselves the glory of eternal life
04_interl4053: because the preachers will be rewarded with the crown of life
04_interl4054: for the diversity of merits, because "star differeth from star in glory".
04_interl4055: because the height of the eternal crown is shown through the four books of the Gospel
04_interl4056: the four fingers signify as many Gospels, because we write with the fingers, and the Spirit by whom the Gospel was written is called the finger
04_interl4057: above the common resurrection of all
04_interl4058: In this is figured the reward of those who excel among the doctors.
04_interl4059: namely of the perfection of life, and of voluntary offering
04_marg1476: AND THOU SHALT MAKE TO IT A LEDGE etc. BEDE. A golden ledge is made on the table round about, because the teaching of the sacred word is ministered through the clean mouths of preachers; nor did the speech of those who handed down the divine secrets consent to be defiled by the words of human chatter, but they bore idle words heavily and reproved them. Or a golden ledge is made to the table round about, because holy Scripture, in every part of its speech, when rightly understood, sounds the brightness of heavenly wisdom. A crown is added to the ledge, because the tongue of the preachers promises the hearers the glory of eternal life. The crown is commanded to be made four fingers high, because the height of the everlasting crown is shown through the four Gospels; or because one must come to the crown of life through keeping the gospel faith and working. And well are the books signified by the fingers, because the tables of the Law were written by the finger of God, and in the Gospel the Lord, about to temper the strictness of the Law, wrote with his finger on the ground, saying: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her. The finger of God is the Spirit of the Lord. Whence what Matthew calls "by the finger of God", Luke, as it were explaining, called "by the Spirit of God". Therefore upon the golden ledge of the table a golden crown four fingers high is set, because the most pure words of the preachers await the hope of the beatitude above, which is contained in the mystery of the Holy Ghost in the four books of the Gospel. Nor do they themselves alone receive the reward in heaven, but they promise the same crown of life to those who obey them, by the sure authority of gospel truth. And the crown is polished, because the eternal kingdom is given to all without difference, but is distributed to each according to the quality of the receivers. But it would not be polished if the brightness of the future reward were opened equally to all; but star differeth from star in glory: so also is the resurrection of the dead; the crown was set on, distinguished with various carvings, but fittingly ordered. For one life is promised to all the just, or a manifold glory of each for the diversity of merits.
04_marg1477: A CROWN etc., AND OVER THE SAME ANOTHER CROWN. BEDE. A golden crown is added when through the Gospel eternal life is promised to those who keep the commandments: If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments. Thou shalt do no murder. Thou shalt not commit adultery etc. On this a little golden crown is set, when it is said: If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast etc. To this crown pertains the new canticle which the virgins alone sing before the Lamb, and they who follow him whithersoever he goeth. Or a golden crown is set on the ledge of the table when in Scripture we learn that souls going out of the body receive eternal rewards in heaven. On this a little golden crown is set, when it is said in Scripture that a more sublime glory is kept for it in the receiving back of bodies.
04_interl4060: the books of the Gospel, through faith in which all holy Scripture is read and understood through the whole world
04_interl4063: because we distinguish the divine Scripture in four ways
04_marg1478: OVER EACH FOOT etc. BEDE. The table of the tabernacle has four feet, because the words of the heavenly oracle are taken either historically, or allegorically, or tropologically, that is, morally, or anagogically. History is when a thing is related in plain speech as it was said or done according to the letter: as the people saved out of Egypt, or the tabernacle made in the desert. Allegory, when by mystical words or things the sacraments of Christ and the Church in the present are signified. In words thus: "There shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root"; which is openly to say: The virgin Mary shall be born of the stock of David, and Christ of her stock. In things, as the people saved out of Egypt by the blood of the lamb signifies the Church freed by the passion of Christ from the dominion of the devil. Tropology, that is, moral speech, looks, in open or figurative words, to the instruction and correction of morals. In open words thus: "My little children, let us not love in word, nor in tongue, but in deed, and in truth." In figurative thus: "At all times let thy garments be white, and let not oil depart from thy head." Anagogy, that is, speech leading to higher things, is that which treats in mystical or open words of the rewards to come and of the life to come in heaven. In open words thus: "Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God." Mystically thus: Blessed are they that wash their robes, that they may have a right to the tree of life, and may enter in by the gates into the city; as if it said plainly: Blessed are they who cleanse their thoughts and works, that they may see God, who says: I am the way, the truth and the life; and through the teaching and examples of those who went before may enter into the kingdom of heaven.
04_interl4064: because we who use the books of the Gospel in this life, rise above them by the crown of life in heaven.
04_interl4066: namely let them keep the mind fixed in reading
04_interl4069: to the hearts of the hearers
04_marg1479: THAT THE BARS MAY BE PUT etc. BEDE. The bars are put through the rings to bear up the table, because the doctors, that they may refresh the hearers with the words of sacred Scripture, must fix the mind on the reading of the Gospel, that they may direct all the intention of their interpretation and teaching to its faith and sense, lest they teach anything else to be done and hoped and loved in the Scriptures than what is found in the four books of the Gospel; who, while they refer all the words of Scripture to the faith and love of the Gospel, as it were carry the whole table of God with its loaves and vessels in the four rings.
04_interl4070: because the preachers are strong, corruptible by no rottenness
04_interl4072: various vessels: various distinctions of the word according to the capacity of the hearers
04_interl4074: biting preaching, namely that bites the vices
04_interl4075: phialas, as it were hialas, because glass is called hialim
04_interl4077: namely those who by preaching stir up to prayer: for incense signifies prayer.
04_marg1480: BEDE. The various vessels which are made for offering the libations are the various distinctions of the word according to the capacity of the hearers, because not all things befit all: the wise are to be taught one way, the foolish another; the poor one way, the rich another; the healthy one way, the sick another; the old one way, the young another; men one way, women another; the unmarried one way, the married another; prelates one way, subjects another. Yet all these vessels pertain to the table of the Lord, namely of the tabernacle, and to the offering of libations. For whatever divers things are said for the diversity of the hearers are found in the rule of sacred Scripture, and stir up the hearts of the hearers to offer to the Lord the vows of good works. Whence: Who, thinkest thou, is the faithful and wise steward?
04_marg1481: THOU SHALT PREPARE DISHES etc. What is understood by the bowls and cups but the measure of preaching, namely that it be given to each according to the capacity of his wit? For he who teaches ought finely to see to it that he does not strive to preach more than is grasped by the hearer. He ought also to draw himself in to the weakness of the hearers, lest, while he speaks sublime things to the little, and therefore things that will not profit them, he care more to show himself than to profit the hearers. And at the Lord's command not only bowls but also cups are prepared for the table of the tabernacle. In the bowls is signified abundant preaching, in the cups the least and slender. On the table of the Lord therefore are bowls and cups, because in the teaching of the sacred word not only are great and secret things to be shown, which delight, but also small and slight things, which give knowledge as it were by a taste.
04_marg1482: One, full of the teaching of truth, inebriates the hearers and as it were holds out a bowl; another cannot fully set forth what he perceives, but because he declares it in some way, gives a taste through a cup. They therefore who cannot minister bowls through the teaching of wisdom, let them give their neighbours to drink cups of the word, as far as they are able by the divine bounty.
04_interl4082: the apostles, or all the doctors who succeed them
04_interl4083: spiritual doctors, who meditate on the Law day and night, and offer the refreshment of the word to all who enter the Church
04_interl4084: because the word of salvation ought always to be open to all
04_marg1483: AND THOU SHALT SET UPON etc. Josephus says twelve loaves were made of fine flour, each of two tenths, which on the sabbath were set upon the table, six on this side and six on that: upon each a golden dish with a handful of incense, and so they were kept until the next sabbath, on which the incense was burned; and the priests ate the loaves, setting out hot ones with incense in their place.
04_marg1484: AND THOU SHALT SET UPON THE TABLE LOAVES etc. They are well called loaves of proposition, because the word of salvation ought always to lie open to all the faithful, nor ought the word of comfort ever to be lacking in the Church: which the Lord, setting it before the world through the heralds of truth, willed to appear in his sight, and to abound unceasingly even to the end for those who hunger and thirst after justice.
04_interl4086: the Church, which shows the light of the word by preaching and doing
04_interl4088: by the hammers of the passion
04_interl4089: because he took up our nature without fault
04_interl4090: the Church, which stands free amid adversities
04_interl4092: This is Christ, the head of the Church, "the mediator of God and men", from whom the whole body, compacted, makes increase unto the increase of God.
04_interl4093: because they inebriate the hearers with the wine of knowledge
04_interl4094: who are always rolling, and are slowed neither by prosperity nor by adversity
04_interl4095: because after all things follows the fatherland, which flowers with the flowers of souls
04_interl4097: because all the virtue and glory of the saints is from God
04_marg1485: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO A CANDLESTICK etc. GREGORY. The candlestick is Christ, in whom the nature of humanity shone with the light of the godhead, that he might become the candlestick of the world, by whose light the sinner might know his own darkness. Of the purest gold, because he took up our nature without fault. And beaten work is drawn out by striking; because Christ from his conception and birth was perfect God and man, yet he bore the pain of the passions, and so came to the glory of the resurrection, and according to the body advanced through the insults of the passion to immortality. For according to the merit of the soul he had nothing at all in which he could advance. But in his members, which we are, he advances daily by passions, because while we are beaten and advance, we deserve to be his body. He advances, of whose body it is said: the shaft thereof and the branches etc. For the shaft is the Church, which is his body, because amid so many adversities it stands free. The branches which come out of the shaft are the preachers, who have sent forth a sweet sound to the world, that is, the new canticle. The cups are the mouths of the doctors, who inebriate us with the wine of knowledge, that we may forget the delights of the world which we loved. The bowl is the rolling swiftness of preaching: for a sphere rolls at all times, and preaching is neither slowed by adversity nor lifted up by prosperity: strong amid adversities, humble amid prosperity, it has neither the corner of fear nor the brow of elation. And well are the lilies described after the cups and bowls, because after the inebriation and swift rolling of preaching follows that green fatherland, which flowers with holy souls, that is, with eternal flowers. The cups therefore and the bowls pertain to labour, the lilies to reward.
04_marg1486: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO A CANDLESTICK etc. The candlestick of the tabernacle, as the table, signifies the universal Church of the present time. For this reason they are before the veil, within which the ark was set, because it has not yet deserved to be brought in to the vision of the Redeemer. It is a table, because to those "who hunger and thirst after justice" it gives daily heavenly food, that they may not fail. It is a candlestick, because it shows the way of light to those who stray, that is, the lamp of the word: and while it humbly subjects itself to this lamp, namely to do the things which the word of God commands, abstaining from pleasures, and to hope and love the things it promises, lifting itself from visible joys, it is made as it were a candlestick, because it sets the heavenly kingdom before its pleasures in all things, and shows the brightness of the word of God to all by preaching and doing.
04_marg1487: AND THE BRANCHES etc. BEDE. Namely the preachers coming out of the shaft, who, appointed by the Lord, sent forth a sweet sound, that is, the new canticle, to the world. The branches are also all the sons of the Church, who, obeying the Prophet who says: "Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle" etc., resound in the praises of the Lord: "He hath directed my steps, and he put a new canticle into my mouth" etc. But by the cups, which are filled with wine, the hearers are signified, who at the voice of the preachers are filled with the wine of knowledge; and because their hearts, inebriated with the wine of inward love, make for God with untiring desire. After the cups the bowls are made. For a sphere rolls on every side, and the minds of the elect are corrupted neither by adversity nor by prosperity, but through holy desires advance in all things. And well are the lilies formed on the branch after the branches and cups and bowls: because after the grace of preaching, after the inebriation of the spiritual drink, after the irrevocable course of holy working, the green fatherland follows, which flowers with holy souls, that is, with eternal flowers.
04_interl4100: who were to preach the faith of the holy Trinity
04_interl4101: for the three times of the world: before the Law, after the Law, under grace
04_interl4102: who after the incarnation preach the same faith openly
04_interl4103: who shall be found in the bed, in the field, or at the mill on the day of judgment
04_marg1488: SIX BRANCHES etc. BEDE. The number six, in which the world was made, designates perfection. Three branches shall come out of one side, and three out of the other, because there were doctors before the coming of the Lord who designated the faith of the Trinity mystically, and preached it as far as the rude could grasp. Whence: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth." There are also now those who preach it openly, so that all who belong to Christ attain the same faith, according to that: "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." Whence Paul: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the charity of God, and the communication of the Holy Ghost be always with you all."
04_marg1489: GREGORY. Again three branches go out from one side and three from the other, because before and after the incarnation there were in the Church three grades of the faithful: of the married, of the continent, and of rulers. Whence Ezechiel foretold that only three men, namely Noe and Daniel and Job, would be delivered. For in Noe, who steered the ark on the waves, he shows the rulers of the Church; in Daniel, who lived continently, the continent or virgins; in Job, who gave an example of patience in married life, the life of the good. These are they who, according to the Gospel, shall be found in the bed, in the field, and at the mill on the day of judgment, of whom one each shall be taken, one each left. For in the bed is the rest of the continent; in the tilling of the field, the industry of the preachers; in the turning of the mill, the labour of the married. And because in all some are to be chosen, some to be rejected, it is said of each: One shall be taken, and the other left. But because the merit of the preachers is higher than that of the continent, and of the continent than of the married, the topmost branches that go out on either side signify the doctors; the lower, the continent; the lowest, the married. They come out of the shaft therefore at divers places, yet all, each in its place and order, bending upward, reach one summit, so as to keep an equal setting of the lamps above them; because, though distinguished by grades of merit, yet imbued with one faith of truth, they are to come to one light of truth in heaven; and the more closely one has taken care to cleave to Christ in this life, the nearer will he enjoy his vision.
04_marg1490: Who, desiring to be filled with the wine of wisdom, form themselves also after the pattern of those who went before, whom they know to have been full of the sweetness and love of invisible goods. The three cups, and bowls, and lilies on each branch signify the three times in which the elect lived devoutly to God before the incarnation and after: before the law, under the law, and in the time of the prophets. After the ascension also the primitive Church was gathered from Israel, now from the gentiles, at the end from the remnants of Israel. The first branch on one side has three cups, bowls and lilies, because the part of the doctors before the incarnation had three orders of those who either thirsted for the draught of grace like cups, or ran in the way of God like bowls, or awaited the gift of the reward on high like the whiteness and fragrance of lilies: that is, before the law, under the law, and under the prophets. The second branch also has the same, because the continent of that time had three orders of saints with the same distinction of times.
04_marg1491: AS IT WERE NUTS etc. The nut signifies the Church. Whence: He went down into the garden of nuts. For the nut has a sweet fruit within, which is not shown unless the shell is broken: so the life of the saints keeps the sweetness of grace in the heart, which is not known outwardly until, the dwelling of the flesh being loosed, the souls behold themselves in the heavenly light.
04_marg1492: The third branch likewise has three cups and bowls, and three lilies, because there were many married before the law, under the law and under the prophets, who rejoiced to hear the word of the Lord, to run his way, and to await the rewards of good works.
04_marg1493: Again. On the other side the first branch, the second and the third had cups and bowls; they had also three lilies, because in each Testament, among the doctors, the continent, and the married devoted to God, there were three orders by distance of times: namely in the primitive Church from Israel, in our election from the gentiles, in the last gathering of the remnants of Israel; who all in their time desire to be inebriated with the word of life, to hasten in the way of peace, to see the whiteness of perpetual light.
04_interl4104: because the Lord gave the cup of wisdom to drink, showed and gave the course of good working, and opened the entrance of the heavenly fatherland
04_interl4106: Christ, of whose grace all receive
04_interl4107: The books of the Gospel, which give us the wine of wisdom to drink and instruct us for the course of good work, that we may attain the lilies, that is, the eternal reward.
04_marg1494: AND IN ITSELF etc. BEDE. We have said that the candlestick itself, that is, the middle stem of the candlestick, from which the branches come out, signifies Christ, of whose grace the just have received whatever good they have. Whence: "I am the vine, you the branches" etc. As if: I am the candlestick, you the branches. As the branch cannot raise itself to bear up the lamp unless it is fixed in the stem of the candlestick, so you too, unless you abide in me, cannot bear the light of truth and faith. In the candlestick are four cups, because in the four books of the Gospel written of the Lord we find the taste of the new wine, that is, of the teaching, which not old bottles, that is, minds still earthly, but hearts renewed by the Spirit receive.
04_interl4108: because the hearts of the saints are held up by the Lord's gifts, commands and promises
04_marg1495: AND BOWLS TO EACH etc. BEDE. There are bowls and lilies together to each cup, because the same Lord who gave the cup of spiritual wisdom to drink also showed the unstumbling course of working, and gave that we might have it, and, that we might not run in vain, promised the brightness of the heavenly fatherland, and by his grace opened its entrance to us. Or because cups, bowls and lilies are commanded to be made under two branches in three places, we can say that to the three grades of the faithful, the married, the continent, the virgins, he opened the teaching of truth, obtained the course of working, and promised and gave the blessing of the unfading inheritance. Fittingly too the cups, bowls and lilies are commanded to be not above the branches but under the branches: because the hearts of the preachers, nay of all the elect, are held up by the Lord's gifts, commands and promises, lest they slip down to the lowest things, and are raised up to love heavenly things. Whence: "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me."
04_marg1496: The cups, bowls and lilies are under two branches, because in each Testament, to the faithful, though differing in ceremonies, the same commands of serving the Lord, the same glory of the heavenly kingdom, were kept. But the fourth cup, sphere and lily, which were above all the branches at the top of the candlestick, pertain properly to Christ, who not only gives the elect the knowledge and working and reward of the virtues, but also showed in himself the figure of the cup, when he showed himself full of the Holy Ghost; and of the bowl, when he "rejoiced as a giant to run the way"; and of the lily also, when, ascending to heaven, he was glorified with the Father. Well does this cup, sphere and lily stand out higher than the branches, because the gifts which God conferred on Christ transcend every measure of human capacity: for to every one is given grace according to the measure of the giving of Christ. But in him dwelleth all the fullness of the godhead corporeally.
04_interl4109: because all the spiritual graces and gifts of the Church are from Christ
04_interl4111: stretched out by the hammers of tribulations
04_interl4112: because Christ himself was free from sin and renowned for works of justice, whom the members imitate in their measure
04_marg1497: AND BOTH THE BOWLS etc. BEDE. The whole work of the candlestick, that is, the stem and the branches coming out of it, with all its adornment, is made of gold, because Christ himself appeared in the world free from sin and renowned for works of justice, whose innocence and justice his members imitate in this life as they can. In the future, by cleaving to him, they will truly bring it to perfection. He himself was beaten gold: for beaten work is drawn out by striking; and our Redeemer, perfect God and man from his conception and birth, bore the blows of the passions, and so came to the glory of the resurrection. And all who will live godly in him suffer persecution, to be enlarged by the blows of the passions to the glory of immortality. Whence: "In tribulation thou hast enlarged me."
04_interl4113: the gifts of the Holy Ghost, which in the night of this world light up the darkness of blindness
04_interl4114: namely lamps, where the oil was lit
04_interl4115: whence: "The spirit of the Lord is upon me"
04_marg1498: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO LAMPS etc. BEDE. The seven lamps are the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, which always remained in Christ and are distributed to the faithful according to his will: these are set upon the candlestick, because the Spirit of wisdom and understanding rested upon him.
04_interl4116: whence: "to heal the contrite of heart, and to preach a release to the captives".
04_interl4117: The table was set in the northern part or quarter; but the candlestick over against it in the southern part, not straight across but obliquely.
04_marg1499: TO GIVE LIGHT OVER AGAINST etc. BEDE. Whence: "To heal the contrite of heart, and to preach a release to the captives" etc. The lamps of the candlestick lit up the tabernacle over against them when Christ, full of grace and truth, gave to all of his fullness: committing the word of the Gospel to the meek and poor, bestowing the remedy of pardon on the penitent; affirming that now is the time of sparing, in the future the time of the universal judgment.
04_interl4119: namely the tongs with which the wicks were snuffed that they might give better light
04_interl4121: namely the vessels, which are the bodies and hearts of the saints
04_interl4123: because the divine words and the grace of God enlighten the hearts of the saints
04_interl4124: because the things then done carnally now, in the spirit, have otherwise a divine brightness
04_marg1500: THE SNUFFERS etc. BEDE. The words by which it is plainly signified in very many things that not the letter of the Law but the spiritual sense is to be kept. Whence: If you be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
04_marg1501: The snuffers, and the vessels where what is snuffed is put out, are made of the purest gold, because divine are the words by which the ceasing of the ceremonies is preached, and enlightened by the grace of God are the hearts in which the shadow of the Law came to its end, that the truth of the Gospel succeeding might shine more clearly. For it is plain that the apostles before the passion loosed the sabbath, and after the Lord's ascension and the coming of the Holy Ghost put an end wholly to the legal victims. In these therefore the wicks that were snuffed were put out; in these the literal observance, fulfilled, showed the beginning of grace more clearly to the world. Again, when mortal life is ended and immortal succeeds, the works or gifts of light which we now use will in the greatest part cease, that the rewards of eternal light may follow in the presence of the divine vision; namely the Scripture which testifies that these things will be. The snuffers are golden with the hope of future brightness; the excellent vessels in which what is snuffed is put out are the immortal bodies and hearts of the saints. And therefore they are likened to gold, in whom this change will be made, that after the temporal benefits of God they may come to the eternal. The Apostle offers as it were golden snuffers and vessels for the differences of present and future goods, saying: "Whether prophecies shall be made void, or tongues shall cease" etc.
04_marg1502: THE SNUFFERS ALSO etc. There are certain precepts in the Scriptures to be kept perpetually both in this life and in the future. (For example:) "Thou shalt not have strange gods before me" and: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart" etc. There are others which are commanded to be kept all the time of this life, that the reward may be rendered in the future. As that: "Make unto you friends of the mammon of iniquity" etc. There are others which, kept in the Old Testament at the Lord's command, are now, the Gospel shining forth, observed not according to the letter but in the mystical sense, as the sabbath, the rite of victims, and the like; which, kept in their time by the people of God, burned like wicks in the lamps of the candlestick, steeped in the oil of devotion, lit by the fire of the heavenly word. But when it was preached by the apostles that all these were ended, and yet were to be kept spiritually, the wicks of the candlestick were snuffed, that, renewed, they might give better light; because, understood more loftily, they give the light of saving doctrine. Of the renewal of the lamps, that is, the loftier understanding of Scripture, it is said: You shall eat the oldest of the old store, and, new coming on, you shall cast away the old. And elsewhere: "Behold, I make all things new."
04_interl4128: which is the greatest among weights and signifies the perfection of Christ and the Church.
04_marg1503: THE WHOLE WEIGHT etc. BEDE. That is, the whole body of Christ with him, namely all the elect, from the highest to the lowest; because all, though in divers grades, ages, sexes, cleave with fixed mind, in their time and place, to one and the same author of perpetual light, as to the golden candlestick, that they may become partakers of the same light. A talent is a full and perfect weight, because "The Lord is just in all his ways"; and he who gives grace to his faithful that they may work well also renders the crown of justice. To the reprobate also he renders according to their works. But they who shine like gold with good works advance into the candlestick of the Lord, because they become partakers of the glory of the Creator. But they who appear in the judgment heavy with sins like lead sink as lead in the mighty waters, who for the merit of their crimes fall into the abyss of the weighing punishment.
04_interl4129: the manifold sacraments of Christ and the Church
04_interl4130: the angelic conversation and the humility of voluntary service
04_marg1504: LOOK AND MAKE etc. The pattern of the candlestick which he was to make was shown to Moses on the mountain, because in the height of contemplation he learned the manifold sacraments of Christ and the Church, which he did not wish to set forth openly to the rude people, but signified in the work of the candlestick and its vessels, until Christ should come, who would reveal the sense of the figures. Whence by dying he rent the veil of the temple, and opened the secrets of the holy places which had been covered; to the disciples also he opened the understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures. For every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven, when he has learned in the holy writings the things of the catholic faith and of pious action, is commanded himself to do them and to teach others; is bidden to look and make according to the pattern that was shown him on the mountain. For he looks diligently at the pattern, namely that shown, and returning to the lower places makes according to it, when he searches with careful heart the things which through the loftiness of the divine word he understands within as to be believed and done, and shows the pattern of these to his hearers by the carrying out of the work and the word of teaching.
04_interl4131: the Church, in which God dwells
04_interl4132: The tabernacle is made with curtains of divers colours, because the universal Church is of many persons, many churches, and various virtues.
04_marg1505: THE TABERNACLE IN THIS MANNER etc. BEDE. The tabernacle which Moses made in the wilderness, and the temple which Solomon made in Jerusalem, signify the state of the universal Church, which partly reigns with the Lord in heaven, partly is absent from the Lord on earth. The tabernacle signifies the building of the Church which is exercised in labours; the temple, the rest to come, which is daily being completed by souls passing thither; because Moses built the tabernacle for the people of God while it was going to the land of promise, but Solomon built the temple in the land of promise when he had gained the kingdom. Moses in the wilderness, Solomon in Jerusalem, which is interpreted 'vision of peace': because here the Church is built in the labour of passing life, in thirst and hunger for the kingdom; there it is perfected in the vision and possession of true peace. Whence in the building of the temple it is said that neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard, the stones and timbers being prepared outside Jerusalem and fittingly shaped, which, set there most easily in their place, were joined either with mortar or with nails: because in the peace of beatitude faith is not to be tried by tribulations, nor life proved; but what has been chastened here and fitted for the seats of heaven is there to be coupled one to another in the sight of the Creator and King, never to be loosed, with the glue and bonds of mutual charity. For when in this life the multitude of believers is of one heart and one soul, and all things are common to them, the living stones are squared for the building of the future house of the Lord, that they may be set in their orders without the labour of delay, and joined by the bond of divine and mutual love.
04_marg1506: The figure of the two sanctuaries can be distinguished thus: that the work of the tabernacle signifies the time of the synagogue, the work of the temple the Church which came to the faith after the incarnation; because Moses made the tabernacle with the Hebrew people alone, but Solomon made the temple with a multitude of proselytes, king Cyrus too helping with his craftsmen, who was a Jew neither by nature nor by profession. For the former people of God had doctors from their own nation only; but the Church had them first from the Hebrews, afterward, as it grew and spread, from the gentiles also, as Luke, Timothy, Titus. But the building of both houses paints, with a wonderful variety of figures, the state of the whole present Church, which does not cease to be built from the beginning of the world to the last just man, and the glory of the life to come, which it now enjoys in part, and after the end of the world will enjoy for ever in all its members.
04_interl4134: because all the perfection of the Church has stood in the love of God and neighbour alone, which is comprehended in the decalogue of the Law; nor is he a member of the Church who does not love him by whom it is built and those in whom, that is, God and his elect
04_interl4135: with the beauty of the virtues; whence: "For the fine linen are the justifications of saints." And elsewhere: "Fine linen and purple is her covering"; for because it springs from the earth, but by long working loses its grassy colour and takes on a white one, it signifies bodies shining with the beauty of chastity, of which it is said: "Know you not that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost?"
04_interl4136: with the love of God and neighbour
04_interl4137: with the burning love of the saints
04_marg1507: OF FINE LINEN etc. BEDE. In these four colours of the curtains four justifications are expressed. In the fine twisted linen: the flesh shining with chastity. In the violet: the mind desiring things above. In the purple: the flesh subject to passions. In the scarlet twice dyed: namely the mind shining forth amid passions with the love of God and neighbour.
04_marg1508: The fine linen is twisted for the curtains of the tabernacle, because the loins of flesh and mind are to be girt, that the flesh may be bridled from wanton motions, and the heart from thoughts.
04_marg1509: Violet, of the colour of the air and the sky, signifies the minds of those who with all their desire cherish heavenly things. Purple, of the colour of blood, and made from the blood of shellfish, figures hearts devoted to God and ready to die for God.
04_interl4139: the long-suffering patience of the Church
04_interl4140: the breadth of charity, which loves even the enemy
04_interl4141: which are the four books of the Gospels, in which charity is taught to be held by the examples and words of Christ, and the four virtues by whose working it is exercised
04_marg1510: THE LENGTH OF ONE CURTAIN etc. BEDE. If you count all the numbers in order from one to seven in full order, you will make up twenty-eight. For one, and two, and three, four, and five, and six, and seven, make twenty-eight. Because therefore the twenty-eighth is found in the parts of the number seven, the length of the curtains is deservedly contained in it; because the faith and patience of the saints, distinguished by variety of virtues, in all that it does or suffers awaits not the glory of human favour but the beatitude of the rest above. Hence it is that the twenty-eighth psalm is written of the completion of the tabernacle, which is sung of the perfection of the Church. Whence: "Adore ye the Lord in his holy court" etc. And: "And in his temple all shall speak his glory." Because in this is the perfection of the Church on pilgrimage, that through faith and good works it make for rest.
04_interl4142: "one Lord, one faith", though the virtues of the saints are divers
04_marg1511: ALL THE CURTAINS SHALL BE OF ONE MEASURE etc. BEDE. Though the curtains differed in their varied embroidery, yet all were tempered to one measure of length and breadth; because though the elect have differing gifts, yet there is "one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all".
04_interl4143: the saints of the Old Testament
04_interl4144: in the setting up of the tabernacle, that one covering may be made
04_interl4145: the saints of the New Testament
04_interl4146: with the same piety and chastity
04_marg1512: FIVE CURTAINS SHALL BE JOINED etc. BEDE. Josephus relates that the tables of the Testament were so written with the decalogue of the Law that each table contained five words. Whence also the ten curtains, which, joined, completed the beauty of the tabernacle, were at the fitting time so disjoined that five remained together on each side; that the ministers of the holy places, beholding these, might be admonished together with the people of the Law always to be kept, which was comprised in ten words on two tables, but distinguished by the number five on each.
04_marg1513: Or the first five, which protected or made the front and first part of the tabernacle, signified the ancient people of God, which fulfilled the decrees of the law according to the letter in the sacrament of circumcision, of victims and of ceremonies. But the following five, which covered or made the hinder parts, designated us, who after the Lord's coming keep the sacraments of the law spiritually, he himself revealing them. All the curtains were of one work, and painted with the same colours, but joined five by five: because all the worshippers of both Testaments believed in one God, and served with the works of one piety and chastity, but in the celebration of the sacraments each people did its own part. For the sacrament of the passion, by which both of us have been redeemed, they celebrated in the flesh and blood of victims, we in the offering of bread and wine. They believed and confessed the birth, passion and resurrection to come; we, as already done and not to be done again. But when the tabernacle was set up, all the curtains were joined to one another; because when the whole beauty of the Church from the beginning to the end of the world is weighed, the tabernacle of the Lord is adorned as by one joining of the ten curtains.
04_interl4147: violet, of the colour of the air, signifies heavenly things
04_interl4148: in the common life and working of the saints
04_interl4149: because we all have the end of temporal life, we hold in common the certainty of the same hope
04_marg1514: LOOPS OF VIOLET etc. BEDE. The curtains are joined to one another by loops of violet when the united hope of the beatitude above joins the hearts of all the saints in one devotion. These loops are fitly said to have been made not only in the sides but also in the tops, that is, at the extreme ends of the corners: because not only do the life and works of the saints hasten to perfection on the common road of right intention, but the beginning of good conversation, which is carried on through the confession of faith and the receiving of the heavenly sacraments, is not different from one another; and with equal grace of truth all have the end of this life joined in the same hope, when they so close their eyes in death that, having first received the viaticum of the heavenly mystery, they trust they will come the sooner to the true life, and will abide in it for ever.
04_marg1515: It is commanded also that fringes be made at the corners of the cloaks, and ribbons of violet, because the elect who desire to see God so clothe themselves with works of justice that they seek their reward not from men but from God. Whence it is added there: That when they see them, they may remember the commandments of God, and not follow their own thoughts etc. The curtains also are joined with loops of violet, that they who see may remember the heavenly commandments; and we, reading thus, may know that, living here as sons of the eternal promise, we are separated by times and places, but in the heavenly fatherland, gathered from the four winds, we shall be joined in an indivisible fellowship.
04_interl4150: for the grace of the Holy Ghost, or the joy of the rest to come to which they make
04_interl4153: toward those who have gone before us or are to follow
04_interl4154: when the just are joined by a concordant multitude of virtues, or by charity
04_interl4155: because the virtues of the saints agree with one another, as the chaste with the chaste, the merciful with the merciful
04_marg1516: FIFTY LOOPS etc. BEDE. In the fiftieth year, namely the jubilee, that is, remitting or begun, according to the law, all the people rested from all labour of the land, and the debts of all were loosed. In the New Testament also, the grace of the Holy Ghost on the day of Pentecost, namely on the fiftieth day of the Lord's resurrection, came upon the apostles and by its coming consecrated the beginnings of the Church. In this number therefore either the grace of the Holy Ghost, or the joy of the beatitude to come, to which one comes through the same Spirit, and in the receiving of which there is true rest and joy, is rightly figured.
04_marg1517: The curtains have fifty loops, because it is brought about by the gift of the Holy Ghost that the elect are coupled to one another in the fellowship of peace, which is the bond of perfection: the hope also of the future, and the remembrance of the fellowship and peace which is had in this life, make those separated by times or places concordant in one piety.
04_marg1518: The curtains have them on both sides, that each may embrace the curtains next to it on either side, as with arms stretched out this way and that. Because it is needful that we embrace with the meeting arms of piety the faithful who went before us in Christ and those who have followed; and that we reverence with one affection in Christ both those who instructed us in Christ and those whom we have instructed. For so ought we to hasten by living well to the face of the Creator, that we do not forsake the neighbour running with us, but strive to arrive together: because the curtains too each so went up to the higher parts by the support of the boards, and so shone within and on high with the varied flower of embroidery, that they did not forsake the curtains which were borne up with them, or which, set on high, shone. So therefore let us not forsake the faithful who advance with us in all service, but treat them with worthy reverence. Loop therefore comes against loop, that one may be fitted to the other, when the just are leagued by a concordant quality of virtues.
04_interl4156: In the golden rings it suggests the perpetual brightness and bright perpetuity of the highest rest, because in a ring neither beginning nor end is found.
04_interl4157: that by saving inspiration one Church may be made of all the saints
04_marg1519: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO FIFTY etc. BEDE. This is unfolded more fully when it is said: "He cast fifty rings of gold" etc. The number fifty designates rest in the Holy Ghost. A ring has neither beginning nor end. Gold is more precious than the other metals in brightness. In the fifty golden rings therefore the perpetual brightness and bright perpetuity of the highest rest is expressed. The rings bite the loops of the curtains, that one tabernacle may be made of all, when the glory of the kingdom above pours itself into the minds of the faithful, so that by such a glue of inspiration one Church of Christ may be perfected from both peoples, nay from all the elect.
04_interl4158: because they humbly confess themselves sinners
04_interl4159: the rulers, by whom the curtains are defended from rain and heat
04_interl4160: as though they neither keep the precepts of the decalogue nor receive the apostolic grace
04_marg1520: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO CURTAINS etc. BEDE. This is found in what follows thus: "He made also eleven curtains of goats' hair" etc. The curtains with which the tabernacle is covered are the rulers, by whose industry and labour the beauty of the Church is ever protected and fortified, lest the life and faith of the saints be corrupted by heretics, or befouled by the wickedness of false catholics, or defiled by the filth of vices, or saddened by want of temporal things. And the more attentively they bear and repel the violence of temptations, the more they give to those subject to them the freedom of serving the Lord; and they give the curtains within as it were the means of shining, while like hair curtains they bear the storms without.
04_marg1521: They signify the coarse minds of men, which by the hidden judgment of God, though hard, are set over others, because they do not fear to serve temporal cares, so as to bear the winds and rains of temptation.
04_marg1522: THOU SHALT MAKE ALSO CURTAINS etc. Haircloth belongs to penitents. Whence: "But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, I was clothed with haircloth", that is, the habit of penance and humility, by which, being calm, I might either bear the fury of the persecutors more lightly, or soften it. For if goats' hair or goats' skins always signified the stench of penitents, the animal itself would not be counted among the clean, nor would it be said in praise of the bride: "Thy hair is as flocks of goats" etc. The curtains therefore, which signify the holy preachers, are of haircloth, and are eleven, because the more zealously they purify their hearts, the more things they find for which to reprove themselves. Whence they humbly confess: For in many things we all offend; and: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves etc. Yet of how great perfection their hearts are is declared when it is said: "The length of one hair curtain" etc.
04_marg1523: The curtains are of haircloth, or of goats' hair, and are eleven. For the preachers, the higher in merit, the humbler in mind, according to that: The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things. For the number eleven, which passes ten and does not reach twelve, that is, the apostolic number, signifies transgression of the decalogue. In the eleventh psalm also the Prophet complains, saying: "Save me, O Lord, for there is now no saint" etc.; silently designating by this number that men of this kind, double in tongue and heart, neither keep the precepts of the decalogue nor receive the apostolic grace.
04_marg1524: There are eleven veils of hair, that is, of haircloth. For in sins there is transgression, which is signified in the number eleven, which transgresses ten, that is, the law: therefore eleven multiplied by seven make seventy-seven, in which the Lord signified all remission, saying: I say not to thee, till seven times, but till seventy times seven times. As many generations are found when Luke, numbering from the Lord's baptism, goes up toward the beginning and comes through Adam to God. For the signifying of sins is made in these garments for this, that they may be expressed through confession, and abolished and covered through the grace which is given to the Church. Whence: "Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered."
04_marg1525: To cover the top, namely, lest the tender, bright things within be troubled by any adversity; otherwise neither does the fine linen shine, nor the scarlet glitter, nor the violet be adorned with its sky colour. They therefore who advance in the bosom of the Church ought not to despise those set over them if they see them taken up with outward things.
04_interl4165: because they perfect the decalogue of the law in the faith of the holy Trinity
04_interl4166: the breadth of sincere charity, which is commended in the four Gospels
04_marg1526: BEDE. The length has the number ten, and this tripled, by which is indicated the virtue of those who perfect the decalogue of the Law in the faith of the holy Trinity which worketh by charity: than which perfection none can be higher in this life. The breadth of four cubits, by which the breadth of sincere charity, as it were in a sign, is commended and expressed. The eleven curtains of goats' hair therefore cover the top of the tabernacle. So in length they have thirty cubits, in breadth four, because those highest preachers, who protect the life of the faithful by exhorting and interceding with daily care, by watchings, fastings and their own nakedness, who, having contemplated the excellence of purity above, confess themselves sinners, but according to the human measure are raised high among men.
04_interl4167: because one is the faith by which the Church is saved, and one the eternal life to which it hastens
04_interl4168: namely the masters of the ancient people, who were in the five ages of the world
04_interl4169: the doctors of the New Testament, who take up in aid of preaching all that was said or done in the six ages of the world; or, set in the sixth age, interpret all things spiritually
04_interl4170: the tabernacle was covered with ten curtains; the eleventh was set doubled in the front, lest the lamps be put out by the force of the winds
04_interl4171: at the entrance of the Church
04_marg1527: THE MEASURE SHALL BE EQUAL etc. BEDE. Because one is the faith in which the Church is saved, and one the eternal life to which it hastens. Whence they who entered the Lord's vineyard to work at different times are all rewarded with one penny. The division of the curtains into five and six therefore can be understood as we expounded above of the curtains divided into five and five: because they signify the doctors of both Testaments. The five curtains, namely the masters of the ancient people of God, who preached only the sacraments of the Mosaic law, or because they led their life in the five ages of the world. But the six, the masters of the New Testament: because they take up in aid and example of their preaching all that the divine Scripture relates as done or said in the six ages of the world, and openly proclaim to their hearers that the passion of Christ, by which the world was redeemed on the sixth day of the week, is to be believed and confessed, and testify that there is salvation through it alone. Whence it is commanded that the sixth curtain be doubled in the front of the roof, namely for the confession and imitation of the Lord's passion. For it is not enough for believers to be baptized and consecrated in the confession of the Lord's death and resurrection, unless each one baptized has striven to be made like to the likeness of the Lord's death by living and suffering, that he may become partaker of the resurrection. Indeed according to the letter he calls the front of the roof the entrance of the tabernacle, where not boards but pillars were set, and a bar stretched from corner to corner of the boards: for as far as pertains to the form of the work, there was more need of a doubled defence of curtains where the solid firmness of a wall was lacking.
04_marg1528: Look also at the measure of the curtains with which the house is covered, how they can agree with the aforesaid measures. There were ten curtains, each having twenty-eight cubits of length and four of breadth, which, joined together and made into one, filled the tabernacle with their breadth to forty cubits. Hang up the curtains, therefore, which each have twenty-eight cubits of length, and set them in a house whose measure across is thirty cubits, and you will see that the curtains will have ten cubits each on the level which is between the walls; but in the going up or down, which is beside the walls, they will have nine cubits each. And so it comes about that the edge of the curtains cannot touch the ground, but stays higher by the measure of one cubit from the ground. Again you will see that the curtains have thirty cubits on the level along the length of the house; but in the going up or down, which is on the eastern or western side of the house, five cubits each. And therefore the same side edge of the curtains does not reach to the ground, but stays higher from the ground by five cubits. Whence it becomes necessary that the five cubits of the curtains which are left over where the walls cease be drawn toward each other on the western side and the eastern, and joined to each other; and so it comes about that the curtains cover the house on every side down to the ground, except for one cubit. So much for the curtains.
04_marg1529: The hair curtains have thirty cubits of length each, four of breadth; and because they were eleven, joined to one another by their sides, they filled forty-four cubits. Set these also, therefore, in the house: and because the length of the hair curtains agrees with the cord by which you measured the house across, it comes about that their edge reaches down to the ground. For they had ten cubits each of level between the walls, and ten each of going up or down on either side. And this is what he says, that a cubit hung on one side, another on the other, which was over in the length of the hair curtains, protecting each side of the tabernacle. For he properly calls the tabernacle the very making or joining of the curtains, which the hair curtains passed by one cubit on the south part or side of the house, and by another on the north. And therefore they reached to the ground, because these had thirty cubits of length, those two fewer. Again the measure of the hair curtains along the length of the house was stretched to forty-four cubits, namely having thirty cubits on the level, from the front of the house to the top of the boards on the western quarter, and seven cubits hanging down on the eastern quarter, and seven likewise hanging down on the western quarter. And so it was that the measure of the hair curtains on the western side exceeded the measure of the curtains by two cubits; because the curtains coming down from above covered five cubits of the same western part, and left five untouched. And this is what he now says: And that which shall remain in the curtains that are prepared for the roof, that is, the one curtain which is over, with the half of it thou shalt cover the back parts of the tabernacle. For the half of a curtain in breadth is two cubits: with which half the back parts of the tabernacle were covered, that is, of the curtains which are properly called the tabernacle, because the last hair curtain passed them by two cubits, stretching down to the lower parts. And again the hair curtains coming down from above covered only seven cubits of the western part: yet the three remaining down to the ground did not lie bare to the injuries of storms, but, the hair curtains of seven cubits which were left over where the walls failed being drawn toward each other from either side, by these the back parts of the house were most firmly covered down to the ground. Nor could these only reach to each other and touch each other in the middle of the wall like the curtains, but because they were of seven cubits each, they passed the middle of the wall on either side by two cubits, and were joined laid one over the other; which we think is to be understood in the same way in all things of the eastern part of the house. And therefore it is commanded above that the sixth curtain be doubled in the front of the roof.
